source_name: IT-Integrator (ІТ-Інтегратор) — Ukrainian systems integrator serving banks
why_relevant: Large domestic integrator (20+ years) covering data centres, security and infrastructure — the delivery channel through which many bank IT and payment-infrastructure projects are actually executed. Project/reference pages indirectly reveal bank procurement that never reaches public tender portals.

source_name: AUB / NABU banking-association news on processing migrations
why_relevant: Bank associations republish vendor win announcements (e.g. Oschadbank launching its own processing centre on WAY4; Alfa-Bank Ukraine migrating to a new processing centre). These are dated, bank-confirmed corroborations of vendor claims and the best way to build a migration timeline.

source_name: Company-registry aggregators (YouControl / Opendatabot / SMIDA) for vendor legal entities
why_relevant: Every vendor in this cell has a Ukrainian legal entity with EDRPOU code, filed financials, beneficial owners and, often, public-procurement history. This converts marketing claims into auditable revenue and ownership data — the quantitative backbone for sizing the bank-tech supply market.

source_name: NovaPay — newsroom / financial and transfer volume disclosures
why_relevant: Largest Ukrainian non-bank payment institution (Nova Poshta group). Publishes recurring half-year/9-month/full-year disclosures of transfer counts and transaction volumes in UAH (e.g. 205m transfers and UAH 172bn in H1-2025 per Interfax-Ukraine reporting), plus bond-issue disclosures that force financial detail into the public domain.

source_name: ProCard processing centre (Прокард)
why_relevant: Independent Ukrainian processing centre (historically tied to Concord Bank ecosystem) named as one of the small set of non-bank processors serving Ukrainian issuers/acquirers. Client lists and service pages reveal which banks and PSPs outsource card processing and ATM/POS driving.

source_name: Solidgate — Ukrainian-founded global PSP/acquirer, blog and press
why_relevant: Ukraine-founded payment orchestration/acquiring company; discloses client counts (~350 merchants incl. Rozetka, Bolt, MakeUp) and ~50% YoY volume growth in Forbes.ua interviews. Its blog and conference materials also carry approval-rate and payment-method benchmarks useful as proxies for Ukrainian e-commerce payment behaviour.

source_name: RozetkaPay — acquiring/payment platform of the Rozetka marketplace
why_relevant: Marketplace-born Ukrainian acquirer publishing merchant counts (claims 28k-35k+ Ukrainian businesses) and daily payment-operation counts (~350k/day). Marketing pages are a rare public source of merchant-base and throughput numbers for domestic online acquiring.

source_name: WayForPay — Ukrainian payment gateway
why_relevant: Established domestic online acquiring gateway; volume figures circulating in trade press (order of UAH 25bn over 11 months of 2025) plus published tariff structures make it a usable datapoint for domestic e-commerce payment volume and pricing.

source_name: LiqPay (PrivatBank) — acquiring/payment service
why_relevant: PrivatBank's payment service and, by market share, the dominant Ukrainian online acquiring brand. Tariffs, supported methods and periodic PrivatBank press releases on acquiring turnover make it the anchor datapoint for the domestic acquiring market.

source_name: Fondy — Ukrainian-origin PSP
why_relevant: Ukrainian-founded PSP now serving UA and EU merchants; publishes merchant-facing method coverage and occasional volume/market commentary. Useful for cross-border acquiring flows for Ukrainian merchants relocating or selling abroad.

source_name: Portmone.com — payment service / bill-payment operator
why_relevant: Long-established Ukrainian bill-payment and card-payment operator; its biller directory and service categories are an indirect map of utility/telecom/government payment digitisation, and it is consistently listed among the top domestic payment services by session volume.

source_name: EasyPay and iPay.ua — Ukrainian payment services (terminal + online)
why_relevant: Both combine cash-in terminal networks with online payment services, making them one of the few windows onto residual cash-based payment behaviour (terminal top-ups) alongside card payments. Comparative reviews cite their service-category counts and session volumes.

source_name: UAFIC — Ukrainian Association of Fintech and Innovative Companies (annual fintech catalogue)
why_relevant: Publishes an annual Ukrainian fintech company catalogue and 'Fintech in numbers' studies (produced with NBU, Ministry of Digital Transformation, IFC/SECO support). The catalogue is the single densest enumeration of Ukrainian PSPs, wallets, BNPL and money-transfer startups, with segment counts.

source_name: Bank acquiring product & tariff pages (Raiffeisen, UkrSibbank, Ukreximbank, PUMB, monobank business)
why_relevant: Acquirer tariff and product pages disclose MDR ranges, terminal supply models (own POS vs SoftPOS vs rental), settlement terms and supported schemes. Diffing them over time is the most reliable open indicator of acquiring price competition and of the coming interchange-cap transition.

source_name: Mastercard Ukraine newsroom (uk-UA press releases)
why_relevant: Scheme-level operator publishing Ukraine-specific consumer payment research (digital-card adoption, contactless share, willingness to go cash-free) in Ukrainian. One of very few named, citable sources of behavioural cashless/cash-usage percentages for Ukraine.

source_name: Visa Ukraine — market and tokenisation disclosures (via Visa CEMEA press and Ukrainian media)
why_relevant: Visa discloses Ukraine-specific tokenisation penetration (Ukraine cited among global top-5), card-in-circulation shifts and new product rollouts (Payment Passkey). Complements Mastercard for scheme-side market-share and card-count triangulation.

source_name: Interfax-Ukraine business wire — payment-operator results coverage
why_relevant: The wire that most consistently carries quantified quarterly results from Ukrainian payment institutions (NovaPay transfer volumes and counts, bond issues, revenue/profit). Frequently the only durable public record of an operator's periodic numbers when the operator's own page rotates.

source_name: International money-transfer operators serving Ukraine (Western Union, MoneyGram, RIA, IntelExpress, Welsend, Meest, PrivatMoney) — payout-network pages
why_relevant: MTO payout-network and bank-partner pages reveal which systems are live in Ukraine, through which agents (Nova Poshta, Raiffeisen, KredoBank, Bank Vostok, Ukrgasbank), and the size of the service-point network (Welsend cites 2,300+ points) — a direct read on remittance-channel infrastructure and residual cash payout demand.

source_name: PayAtlas Ukraine country profile (PSP / method landscape)
why_relevant: Merchant-facing country guide enumerating Ukrainian PSPs, local payment methods and compliance/fee context. Useful as a cross-check actor list in English and for identifying which local methods international merchants actually integrate.

source_name: Visa Ukraine Newsroom — Press Releases (uk_UA)
why_relevant: Visa's Ukrainian country press room is the primary publication channel for Visa-branded Ukraine-specific consumer research (Stay Secure, Click to Pay, SME digital-payments studies), contactless-growth claims and market milestones. Scheme-authored, Ukraine-scoped, recurring.

source_name: Visa Ukraine Newsroom (English locale)
why_relevant: English mirror of the Ukrainian newsroom; often the only version carrying full study titles and figures in a machine-friendly form, and useful for cross-checking translated statistics.

source_name: Visa Ukraine Interchange Reimbursement Fees (IRF) disclosure PDF
why_relevant: Scheme-published domestic interchange rate table for Ukraine — the authoritative primary artefact behind every interchange debate figure (0.7%/0.9%/1.2% steps). Regulatory/commercial disclosure obligation makes it recurring and versioned.

source_name: Mastercard Ukraine Domestic Interchange and Service Fees (PDF disclosure)
why_relevant: Mastercard's own intracountry interchange/service-fee table for Ukraine — the counterpart to the Visa IRF PDF. Dated filenames make version tracking straightforward and reveal the exact rate-step schedule.

source_name: НПС ПРОСТІР — official site of Ukraine's national card payment system
why_relevant: The national scheme's own portal: participant/bank lists, acceptance rules, product and co-badging information, and periodic milestone communications. Only first-party source on PROSTIR issuance and acceptance footprint.

source_name: NBU — Payment systems section / register of payment systems and infrastructure operators
why_relevant: The regulator's register of payment systems, participants and payment-infrastructure service operators — the authoritative actor map for which schemes (Visa, Mastercard, PROSTIR, UnionPay, remittance systems) are legally registered in Ukraine and through which participants.

source_name: NBU payment-card market statistics releases (expanded public card-market data)
why_relevant: NBU publishes card counts split BY SCHEME (Mastercard / Visa / PROSTIR active cards), transaction volumes and cashless share — the only official dataset giving scheme-level market share in Ukraine, which the schemes themselves do not disclose.

source_name: NBU news item: NBU, Visa and Mastercard interchange memorandum
why_relevant: Primary documentation of the regulator-scheme interchange memorandum that sets the rate-reduction schedule; anchor document for the whole interchange-regulation storyline and for dating rate steps.
